title: RWB-S9-E1057-APP: the split plan gives this secondary slice no legacy criterion and no build row while the P5 slice of the same key hands the partner criteria to it, no source publishes a partner-by-code read or the code filter of GET /partners, the two refusal reasons and the not-found behaviour are not published, the constraint on partner_code and the panel transition table are not specified, the DP-07 rows cannot be carried in an empty H row, and EP01 wave 1 is earlier than the service wave 4
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R5.6, R5.7, R7.1, R7.2, R7.3 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S9-E1057-APP (ACS empty, H empty, C RWB-P5-E1057-CON, patterns DP01, DP06, DP07, DP09, DP10, DP11, DP13, DP15, DP19); context pack S9 rwb-partner (service row, naming rules, ownership rows: tables partner, partner_instruction and partner_user, 6 REST operations, EV-20 and EV-21, workflow InstructionWorkflow, no job; Architecture v5 slides 2, 4, 5, 8 and 12); legacy RWB-E1-057 sections 1 to 19, section 3, section 12 and section 16; FSD S9 Partner management v3 A1.1 to A1.4, A2.1.3.1 to A2.1.4.4, A2.2.3.1 to A2.2.4.4 and the requirements served; TSD S9 Partner management v2 T1, T2, T3.0 to T3.3, T5.1 to T5.3, T6.1, T6.2, T7, T8, T-A.1 and T-A.2; the P5 slice RWB-P5-E1057-APP sections 1, 5, 7, 12.2 and 16
description: (1) The split plan gives RWB-S9-E1057-APP an empty criteria list and an empty H row, while the P5 slice of the same legacy key states in its sections 1, 7, 16 and 19 that AC2, AC3, AC7, AC9 and AC13 of RWB-E1-057 are proved by RWB-S9-E1057-APP, and the wave 1 harness RWB-ITG-E1057-ITG carries the same five criteria as legacy copies; this story therefore writes ten target criteria of its own, answers the partner half of legacy AC2 and AC7 at component level and claims no legacy criterion (ASM-B2-S9-018-1). (2) No source publishes a partner-by-code read: TSD S9 T-A.1 and the context pack give six operations, of which GET /partners (API-S9-001) lists partners with panel status and score under right R with query type and status only, while the legacy story calls an in-process interface PartnerDirectory.findByCode in its section 12; the read is therefore that operation with one additive optional code filter and no second path (ASM-B2-S9-018-2). (3) TSD S9 T-A.2 publishes errors 401, 403 and 503 for that operation and no not-found error, so an unknown code answers an empty list with 200 and the caller's reason PARTNER_UNKNOWN; the not-found behaviour has no published answer (ASM-B2-S9-018-2). (4) The legacy reasons PARTNER_UNKNOWN and PARTNER_NOT_ACTIVE are values of the intake job record of legacy AC7 and no code list publishes them, and the published Partner element carries no reason property, so this service answers the row and its panel status and the caller renders the reason in MSG-P5-007 (ASM-B2-S9-018-3). (5) No source publishes a constraint or an index on partner.partner_code, so the name and the definition of the lookup constraint carry the placeholder and DP-15 adds no migration (ASM-B2-S9-018-6). (6) No source publishes the transition table of LOV-PANEL, so only the reading of BR4 is stated: ACTIVE admits a file and every other value refuses it (ASM-B2-S9-018-7). (7) DP-07 adds the client library RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and the cross-service row RWB-P3-E1043-CON, which the plan's empty H row cannot carry; the rows are stated in sections 12.2 and 13 and tracked here instead (ASM-B2-S9-018-4). (8) EP01 is wave 1 and the service's Arch v5 wave is 4, so the story keeps wave 1 under R5.6 and one conflict is raised per service and business epic (ASM-B2-S9-018-8).
evidence: Split plan slice RWB-S9-E1057-APP (acs [], H [], C [RWB-P5-E1057-CON], secondary true, lane L-S9-C, wave 1, release 30 November 2026); RWB-P5-E1057-APP sections 1, 7 and 16 (the five partner criteria handed to RWB-S9-E1057-APP and the partner-by-code read declared as a consumed row of a class C dependency with no C row of the plan); TSD S9 T-A.1 (6 operations, API-S9-001 GET /partners Partner portal R first in E2) and T-A.2 (query type and status, Partner[] out, errors 401, 403, 503); legacy RWB-E1-057 section 12 (published interface PartnerDirectory.findByCode with id, partnerCode, partnerType and panelStatus) and AC7 (reasons PARTNER_UNKNOWN and PARTNER_NOT_ACTIVE); TSD S9 T3.1 (DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-016) and T3.2 (LOV-PANEL ACTIVE, ON_NOTICE, SUSPENDED, EXITED; LOV-PARTNER-TYPE eight values); FSD S9 A1.3, A2.1.3.1, A2.2.3.1 and BR-S9-002; context pack service row (schema rwb_partner, base /api/recovery/partner/v1, topic rwb.partner.events.v1, queue rwb-partner, wave 4, Jobs 0) and Architecture v5 slides 8 and 12
area: Business definition, contract, data and dependencies
owner_role: Business lead; solution architect; rwb-partner tech lead; rwb-access owner; programme lead
proposed: Serve the partner panel read as the code filter of the published GET /partners under base /api/recovery/partner/v1 with right R and the scope applied, answer the six published properties from partner in rwb_partner, answer an empty list for an unknown code and the stored panel status for a partner that is not ACTIVE, leave BR4 and the two reasons with the caller, read LOV-PANEL and LOV-PARTNER-TYPE through DP-07, write nothing and publish nothing, keep wave 1 and record the DP-07 rows, the constraint on the partner code, the panel transition table and the criteria assignment of the two slices as open items.
